title: Test failure import needs stable executable evidence, not prose reconstruction
expected_semantics: A failed test result should carry enough structured source/request/reproduction evidence for a debugger to open it without parsing a command line or terminal text.
actual_behavior_limitation: The pinned result schema has structured top-level verdict/classification/provenance/reproduction and ordinary test entries can carry request evidence, but an import cannot proceed when the selected test lacks a source and embedded request. The debugger does not reimplement test assertions.
why_capability_matters: A human should be able to move from what failed to how it failed without reconstructing an invocation that may change the failing execution.
current_workaround: Preserve the full test result under integration.result, require source/request for request-level recording, and retain test classification as test-owned evidence.

host_language_code_required.classification: temporary adapter caused by an identified MNCS pressure
host_language_code_required.why: Python transports the test result and creates a temporary request file; it does not decide the verdict.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Make the existing test-result contract explicitly require stable source/program artifact reference and embedded or content-addressed execution request/reproduction recipe for debuggable failures.
resolution_criteria: The first-class test result has a documented, content-addressed program/request/replay reference for every debuggable failure and import works without command-text parsing.
